title: Everything We Know About The New Tarkov Game
summary: Get an early look at Fragmentary Order, a new game coming from the creator of Escape From Tarkov, including hints at the story, gameplay, and required s...
body_markdown:
Escape from Tarkov has been around for ten years. Ten! And in that past decade, fans of first-person shooters have seen Tarkov revolutionize how we think about the genre. Features like proximity chat, highly modular weapons, and losing all of your items on death were once considered “hardcore” – but now, after Tarkov popularized them, you can see versions of these same features being adopted in many of the best FPS games out there, from Call of Duty to Arc Raiders and everything in between.


After a decade-long reign, it’s safe to say Tarkov fans are due for a new Tarkov-ian experience, and Game Director Nikita Buyanov is here to deliver. Buyanov just uploaded a 14-minute first gameplay trailer for a brand-new game called Fragmentary Order, which is referred to as a “hardcore sci-fi first-person combat simulator.” Here’s how they set up the game in the video description:


“Year 2251. War has been outsourced. You fight through RepEnt, remotely operated clones, across the Solar System. Death is a cost. Risk is an investment. Combat is your labor.”


It’s giving Tarkov in Space.


Indeed, Tarkov players will notice a lot of familiar elements in the gameplay trailer – highly customizable gear (including drones), comms with nearby players, inventory management, looting, and, of course, tense gunplay.


But there are some curiosity-sparking aspects of the trailer as well. For one thing, the scenery is spectacular. Between the distant mountain landscapes, blustering storm winds, and lodgings made from shipping crates, you really get the sense of being on a dilapidated settlement on a distant planet. It really makes you wonder how humans were able to colonize the Solar System, who is waging war on these planets, and why.


While 14 minutes isn’t a ton of time to explore every aspect of gameplay, Buyanov still appears to be planning an ambitious project that goes far beyond what we can already see. "We're not building a match you play,” he says. “We're building a world you live in, for years. Tarkov is still worth playing after ten years, and I want Fragmentary Order to be just as playable and engaging a decade from now."


Well, all of those long-term plans start with a successful testing phase, which is already available on the company’s website. There are two paid packages that get you in:


- Candidates Package: For $44.99, you get alpha access, access to the full game at launch, a beta launch item package, and a candidate designation in the rank system.
- Founders package: You get everything above, plus in-depth and experimental testing sessions, an exclusive look at the development roadmap, and access to a closed dev channel with the opportunity to add offer direct feedback.


If any of you get the Founders package, let the devs know they missed a golden opportunity to call the game “Starkov.”


On the game’s official Twitter, the developer announced that the first closed alpha playtests are scheduled to begin this December. System requirements are roughly as follows:


**MINIMUM**


• CPU: Intel Core i5-13600K / AMD Ryzen 7 5800X


• RAM: 16GB


• GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060, 8GB VRAM


**RECOMMENDED**


• CPU: Intel Core i7-14700K / AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D


• RAM: 16GB


• GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (10GB) / RTX 4070 (12GB) / RTX 5060 Ti (16GB)


Time will tell if Fragmentary Order will be the next big thing in FPS gaming, but there’s no doubt that the[Stealth™ Ultra II](https://www.turtlebeach.com/products/stealth-ultra-ii-controller?Title=Default+Title) is the next big thing in wireless XBOX & PC controllers.


The[Stealth™ Ultra II](https://www.turtlebeach.com/products/stealth-ultra-ii-controller?Title=Default+Title) has everything you need to up your game, like adjustable trigger stops, tactile microswitch buttons, AntiDrift™ TMR thumbsticks, and an ultra-responsive wireless polling rate of up to 1kHz. Not only that, you’re also getting instant access to game-changing customization via the all-new Connected Command Touch Screen, which lets you adjust things like audio tuning, vibration feedback, and button mapping on the fly. Plus, you can deeper with GateShift technology that enable you to fine-tune your analog stick behavior to match how you play. There’s nothing you can’t do with the Stealth™ Ultra II.
